key_insight: IRMAE-WD’s sharp latent singular-value drop identifies the trained representation’s effective dimension, not necessarily turbulence’s intrinsic degrees of freedom.
engineering_relevance: For compact wall-turbulence representations, choose the coordinate count by required reconstruction accuracy or resolved scale rather than a single dimension estimate.
method: Apply IRMAE-WD with a 3D convolutional autoencoder to minimal-channel velocity fields.
Vary the number of linear layers and truncate latent coordinates at the singular-value drop.
Use transfer learning to compare coordinate requirements with POD across reconstruction accuracies and scales.
evidence_signal: At Reτ = 110, truncation at the drop reduced reconstruction rate by at most 0.01 percentage points; with transfer learning, IRMAE-WD needed fewer coordinates than POD up to about 97% reconstruction, but POD needed fewer above that threshold.
watch_item: The drop shifts toward lower dimensions as linear layers are added, so it should not be treated as an architecture-independent intrinsic dimension.
paper_title: Effective-dimension estimation of a minimal turbulent channel flow via IRMAE-WD
